short: Parliament established a moderate Protestant framework for the Church of England.
full:
In May 1559, Elizabeth I's first Parliament officially passed the Acts of Supremacy and Uniformity, collectively forming the landmark Elizabethan Religious Settlement. The foundational legislation completely severed England from Rome once again, declared the new queen the Supreme Governor of the Church, and mandated a revised Book of Common Prayer that deliberately accommodated varying theological views to prevent civil strife.

The settlement effectively concluded the extreme, deadly religious pendulum swings of the mid-Tudor period, successfully forging the distinctive, moderate 'middle way' of Anglicanism. While it deeply dissatisfied both ardent Roman Catholics and radical emerging Puritans, the theological compromise proved remarkably durable, ultimately securing long-term domestic stability and permanently defining the core religious character of the English nation state.
